title: Generalized nonsymmetric cartesian algebras reconstructed from product cones
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $p:\mathcal M\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], with Kan zero fibre and incidence axiom including both vertex and edge projections. Let $B$ be any infinity category with finite products. Let $B^\times\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the pullback of the cartesian symmetric monoidal category of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] along the ordered-block functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$. This functor takes $[r]$ to $\langle r\rangle$ and sends input $i$ to output $j$ if $a(j-1)<i\leq a(j)$ for the opposite ordinal map $a:[s]\to[r]$, and to the basepoint otherwise.

There is a coherent total-product functor $\Pi:B^\times\to B$. On a tuple it takes the finite product, and on an arrow its output components are the block maps precomposed with projections from the full input product; the degree-zero product is terminal. Let $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal M}(B)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M,B)$ on functors $M$ for which the inert projections exhibit
$$M(m)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^r M(m_i)\quad(m\in\mathcal M_{[r]}),$$
including a terminal value on every object over $[0]$. Then composition with $\Pi$ induces an equivalence from the full category of inert-preserving functors $\mathcal M\to B^\times$ over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ to $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal M}(B)$. At $m$ an inverse has tuple $(M(m_1),\ldots,M(m_r))$. On an arrow $m\to m'$ its $j$th block map is obtained by first projecting $m$ to that consecutive block, then applying the induced arrow to $m'_j$, and using the product-cone equivalence for that block. The inverse is a coherent functor, including all transformations and higher simplices, and the space of inverse lifts with the specified product-cone identification is contractible. These assertions are natural under inert-preserving operad maps and finite-product-preserving functors in $B$. No terminality of $\mathcal M_{[0]}$, and no colimits in $B$ or cocartesian lifts of active arrows in $\mathcal M$, are assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.1, Lemmas 5.14-5.15 and Remark 5.16 (cartesian patterns); agent extension to generalized nonsymmetric incidence operads with Kan zero fibre and terminal zero-degree values. The generalized extension is not claimed to be a literal statement of those results. Online PDF read, archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this coherent infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Realize the cartesian envelope by the product-diagram subcategory P of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition], identified with the envelope in [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Its coherent full-subset evaluation is Pi. Pull back along the stated ordered-block functor; pullback preserves the lifting properties in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. The evaluation formula is exactly the product and block-map formula of the statement. If H preserves inert edges, its inert projections are cocartesian in P, so their evaluations are the product projections and Pi H satisfies the required product cones, including terminal values in degree zero. Composition with Pi is a functor on the full functor categories, not just on objects.

source.place: Proposition 5.1 and Lemma 5.15; forward direction using the existing product-diagram model

proof.text: Here is an auxiliary indexing category for constructing the inverse without a hypothesis on the arity-one fibre. Let P_n be the finite path with vertices 0,...,n and edges (i-1,i). A subgraph K consists of a subset of vertices and of edges whose endpoints are included; allow the empty subgraph and isolated vertices. For a monotone map a:[s] to [r], let a_!L be the union of the vertex images and the entire closed intervals [a(j-1),a(j)] for edges (j-1,j) of L. This operation preserves unions and satisfies (ab)_!=a_!b_!: both sides replace each edge by the interval between its composite endpoint images. Form the ordinary category with objects ([r],K), and a single arrow over [r] to [s] when a_!L is contained in K. Its projection to Delta-op is a cartesian fibration: the cartesian lift with target ([s],L) has source ([r],a_!L). Pull it back along p to obtain a quasicategory D. Let I be its full subcategory of nonempty connected subgraphs, namely closed intervals [a,b], including a=b. The same description shows I is a quasicategory, since a_! preserves nonempty intervals. These assertions follow directly from the horn and cartesian-edge definitions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]: the subgraph coordinate in a lift is forced by interval image and containment, and the remaining lifting problem is in M. The full-interval section s:M to I is fully faithful, since every base arrow satisfies its containment condition.

source.place: Agent construction of a path-subgraph indexing category; refinement of the auxiliary diagram argument in Lemmas 5.14-5.15

proof.text: For an interval object t=(m,[a,b]) of I choose an inert cocartesian projection m to m_[a,b] over the opposite of the interval inclusion the ordinal of length b-a to [r]. It gives an arrow t to s(m_[a,b]) in I. For every x in M this arrow induces an equivalence Map_M(m_[a,b],x) to Map_I(t,s(x)). Indeed a base map represented by c:[k] to [r] occurs on the right exactly when its whole image is in [a,b]; it then factors uniquely as the inclusion [a,b] followed by the translated map to the ordinal of length b-a. On each such base-arrow fibre the equivalence is precisely [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The base mapping spaces are discrete, so taking their disjoint union gives the displayed equivalence. The opposite universal-arrow assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] now supplies a coherent left adjoint r:I to M to the fully faithful s, with r(m,[a,b])=m_[a,b], unit t to sr(t), and equivalence rs to id. Thus for F in Mon_M(B), G=Fr is an actual coherent interval diagram. In particular G takes the unit t to sr(t) to an equivalence. This is a construction of coherent interval restrictions, not an assertion that independently chosen operation maps automatically extend to higher simplices.

source.place: Agent generalized extension: coherent inert restriction by cocartesian universality, in place of assuming the cartesian-pattern hypothesis of Proposition 5.1

proof.text: Compute the limit needed to right Kan extend G from I to D. Fix e=(m,K), and let J_e=I times_D D_(e/) be the full coherent comma category of arrows from e to interval objects. Let A_e be its full subcategory whose targets are full intervals s(x). For an object e to t of J_e, the unit eta_t of Step 3 gives an arrow from it to e to t to sr(t), which lies in A_e. Precomposition with this arrow is an equivalence on mapping spaces into every object e to s(x) of A_e: these mapping spaces are the homotopy fibres of Map_I(sr(t),s(x)) and Map_I(t,s(x)) over the given point of Map_D(e,s(x)), and precomposition with eta_t identifies the two total spaces by the universal property of Step 3 and full faithfulness of s, compatibly with the maps to Map_D(e,s(x)). The diagram G|J_e carries each such arrow to G(eta_t), an equivalence by Step 3. Hence [lem-coef-reflection-inverting-limit-restriction] applies: a cone on G|J_e is limiting exactly when its restriction to A_e is, and limits of G|J_e exist exactly when those of G|A_e do. Now A_e is a disjoint union over the connected components C of K. An object e to s(x) represented by c:[k] to [r] belongs to the unique C containing the connected nonempty interval c_!P_k. In its component the inert projection e to s(m_C) is initial: factoring c through C is unique in the base, and the space of lifts of this factorization is contractible by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. There are no simplices between different components, since a triangle keeps its image inside the component of its first arrow. By [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components], applied to B over the point, the limit of G|A_e is the finite product of the values G(s(m_C)), equivalently F(m_C), over the components C of K. If K is empty J_e and A_e are empty and this limit is terminal, as that lemma includes the empty index set. This is an existence proof for the required limits using finite products only.

source.place: Agent comma-category calculation completing the generalized extension of Lemma 5.14

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction] to the full inclusion I in D, with target B over the point. The map B to the point is an isofibration since B is a quasicategory and identities lift the only equivalence of the point. Step 4 supplies every required limit cone. Restriction from such extensions is a trivial Kan fibration, including transformations and prescribed higher boundaries; lifting simplex by simplex along boundary inclusions, starting from the empty simplicial set, it has a strict section sigma from the full subcategory of admissible interval diagrams. Since every Fr with F in Mon_M(B) is admissible by Step 4, put Ghat=sigma(Fr), a coherent right Kan extension of G depending functorially on F. Its value at (m,K) is the product over components C of K of F(m_C). For any component with edges, the product-cone hypothesis on F gives F(m_C) as the product of F(m_i) over those edges, because composite inert projections agree with those from m. For an isolated vertex, F(m_C) is terminal by the degree-zero hypothesis. Thus Ghat(m,K) is canonically the product over edges i of K of F(m_i), with all these identifications respecting their cones. Put E=M times_(N(Fin_*)) N(Gamma^times), where Gamma^times is the subset category in [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]. There is a functor v:E to D sending (m,S) to the graph with all vertices and edges S. For an arrow over a:[s] to [r], the condition a_!(all vertices, edges T) contained in (all vertices, edges S) says exactly that every input in a^{-1}(T) lies in S. Therefore it is exactly the arrow condition in E. The relative-exponential identity of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] turns Ghat v into a coherent functor H_F:M to Q over Fin_*. Its fibre diagrams are product diagrams by the value computation, so it factors through P, and its base factorization gives H_F:M to B^times over Delta-op.

source.place: Agent right Kan extension and relative-exponential construction, following the architecture of Lemmas 5.14-5.15

proof.text: The construction has exactly the advertised block formula. For u:m to m-prime over the opposite of a:[s] to [r], fix output j. The target interval [j-1,j] has image C=[a(j-1),a(j)]. Applying the coherent r to the corresponding interval arrow gives m_C to m-prime_j; the unit of Step 3 identifies its composite from m with the jth inert projection after u. Applying F and the product identification for m_C gives the block map from the product of F(m_i) for a(j-1)<i<=a(j) to F(m-prime_j). The cone computation of Steps 4-5 gives this same map in H_F; the mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition] reads it as the jth block component. When a(j-1)=a(j), m_C is an object over [0] and its F-value is terminal, so this also constructs the nullary operation. If u is inert cocartesian, every target block is a singleton and its induced arrow m_C to m-prime_j is an equivalence: both projections from m are cocartesian over the identical singleton selector, and their universal mapping-space equivalences identify their targets. Applying F therefore gives equivalences on all block maps. The envelope's cocartesian criterion proves H_F preserves inert edges. Here inert means a cocartesian edge over an inert base map, as in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]; no claim is made for arbitrary edges over inert base maps.

source.place: Agent block-map computation and inert check, corresponding to Lemma 5.15; includes vertex blocks

proof.text: On the full-interval section s:M to I to D, the restriction equivalence of the right Kan extension identifies Ghat s with Frs, hence with F. The graph v(m,{1,...,r}) is this full interval. Therefore the relative-exponential evaluation identifies Pi H_F with F, naturally on all of M and on transformations and higher simplices. This is the specified product-cone identification; its naturality follows from the extension's coherent counit, not from choosing equalities on mapping-space components.

source.place: Agent comparison for a product-cone functor, completing the first inverse of Lemma 5.14

proof.text: For the other comparison start with an inert-preserving H and put F=Pi H. Evaluation of H gives a diagram on E. Forgetting the isolated vertices defines w:D to E, (m,K) to (m,edges(K)); the arrow condition holds because the edges of a_!L are exactly the ordered-block inverse image of edges(L). Let T_H:D to B be evaluation composed with w. T_H carries each unit (m,[a,b]) to s(m_[a,b]) to an equivalence: it evaluates the cocartesian edge H(m to m_[a,b]) on a cartesian arrow of Gamma-times, which [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] and [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition] send to an equivalence, including terminal values for a=b. Hence T_H(eta) identifies T_H|_I with T_H s r=Fr=G. T_H is right Kan extended from I: at e=(m,K), T_H also carries the reflection arrows of Step 4 in J_e to equivalences, so by [lem-coef-reflection-inverting-limit-restriction] and [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] its canonical cone is limiting once its restriction to the initial objects s(m_C) is. That restriction is the map from H(m)(edges K) to the product over C of H(m_C)(all edges), which through the product cones of H(m) and these cocartesian transports is the regrouping of the product over the edges of K by components; isolated vertices give terminal factors. So it is limiting. Restriction R to T is an equivalence of full infinity categories with section sigma by [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction], so T_H is equivalent to sigma(T_H|_I), hence to Ghat=sigma(Fr), compatibly with the interval identification. Since wv is the identity of E, T_H v is the evaluation of H and Ghat v that of H_F; applying the bijection of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] to M times Delta^1 turns this equivalence into a transformation from H_(Pi H) to H over Fin_*, whose components are fibrewise equivalences; it is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. All choices are made by functors of H, so this is natural in H.

source.place: Agent comparison for an inert-preserving functor, completing the second inverse of Lemma 5.14

proof.text: Assembly. Composition with Pi is a functor Phi from inert-preserving functors to Mon_M(B) (Step 1). F to H_F is a functor Psi: precomposition with r, the section sigma, restriction along v and the relative-exponential bijection applied to M times Delta^n are all simplicial maps (Steps 3-5). Step 7 gives a natural equivalence Phi Psi to id and Step 8 one from Psi Phi to id; their components are equivalences, so by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] Phi is an equivalence of full infinity categories with quasi-inverse Psi, which has the advertised block formula by Step 6. Contractibility: the space of inverse lifts of a specified F with its product-cone identification is the homotopy fibre of the map of cores induced by Phi over F; Phi induces an equivalence of cores, so this fibre is contractible. Naturality: for an inert-preserving operad map u:M' to M, restriction along u commutes strictly with Phi. For a finite-product-preserving h:B to B', postcomposition with h carries product diagrams to product diagrams, hence P into P' and the pullback B-times into B'-times, preserving cocartesian edges by the block-map criterion of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]; full-subset evaluation commutes strictly with it, so again Phi commutes with h. Because Phi is an equivalence commuting with u and h, the quasi-inverses commute with them up to the canonical equivalences obtained from the unit and counit, with their higher compatibilities. No colimits in B, terminality of M_[0], or cocartesian active lifts are used.

source.place: Agent assembly of the equivalence, contractibility and naturality; compare Remark 5.16

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.1, Lemmas 5.14-5.15 and Remark 5.16 for cartesian patterns; independent agent extension using interval restrictions, path-subgraph comma limits, and right Kan extension. The paper is not asserted to cover the generalized hypotheses verbatim.

split_report.summary: Second reading repairs an inapplicable space-valued-colour operation lemma and unsupported higher-coherence and contractibility claims. Eight steps construct coherent interval restrictions by universal arrows, compute path-subgraph comma limits, right Kan extend, and recover the product-diagram envelope by relative exponentiation. No new nodes or leaves; no statement change. Maintainer reader fix (2026-10-17): the cone retraction along the reflective subcategory A_e, proved inline in Step 4 and repeated in Step 8, is now the statement-only lemma lem-coef-reflection-inverting-limit-restriction; the disjoint-component product is cited from lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components (replacing lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit); the long Step 8 is split into Steps 8 and 9; the off-unit tool uses are declared.
split_report.blueprint: The ancestor prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2 calls for product-cone reconstruction in a cartesian target. Steps 1-8 realize that comparison, including a written generalized extension of the cartesian-pattern source argument.

tool_uses.why: The item explicitly uses quasicategory, coherent mapping-space and universe conventions; these generic notions come from the CBC unit.

Steps 5, 7 and 8 use only its simplicial mapping bijection and its cocartesian-edge criterion to pass between diagrams on M times_Fin* Gamma-times and functors into the relative exponential; the in-unit recognition lemma is itself stated through it and no node of this unit gives the bijection.
Steps 8 and 9 use only that a transformation of coherent diagrams with equivalence components is an equivalence; a generic quasicategory fact, not a replacement for a step of the unit.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q51-92a683545 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 11 cited statements, the unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general (it cites only sk-def-sf-operations and sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation), the chapter, and the main-20261015 proof of the blueprint ancestor prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint. Chu-Haugseng 2006.08269 and HA are not archived locally, so I could not check the cited place; the node marks itself as an agent extension, so I checked the mathematics myself. The statement is true and unchanged: I tested r=0 and r=1, an inert selector and a collapsed block (nullary operation). The checks that matter: the cut functor; a_! preserves unions and (ab)_!=a_!b_!; the cartesian lift and the full faithfulness of s; the coherent left adjoint r through the dual universal-arrow clause, with discrete base mapping spaces; v and w respect arrows because edges(a_!L) is the cut preimage alpha^{-1}(edges L), and wv=id; inert preservation through cocartesian uniqueness; Pi H_F = F r s = F. Duplicate check: lem-coef-lax-cartesian-classification is the symmetric cocartesian case, not a duplicate. Long step 8 (2404 characters) hides a lemma. It says 'repeat the cone retraction R_e of Step 4' for a second functor, and that argument has its own hypothesis: a bare restriction of limits along the final reflective inclusion A_e is false (J={0->1}, A={1}); it works only because the diagram inverts the reflection. It also packs in the assembly, contractibility and naturality. Fixes, three faults: (1) C1/D5: new statement-only node lem-coef-reflection-inverting-limit-restriction (rg and blueprint search found no existing node; Mathlib grep finds only the ordinary-category initial_of_adjunction at Limits/Final.lean:144), cited in Steps 4 and 8; step 8 split into 8 and 9, all steps now under 2000 characters; Step 5 now names a strict section sigma so F->H_F is a functor; Step 9 proves naturality strictly through the product-diagram model.
